For some unknown reason (clear only to Cultured Code) users cannot use natural language to create a task. I want to write “do the thing at 8pm” and for it to create a reminder called “do the thing” with a reminder set for 8pm. But things won’t add the reminder. Instead, it will name the task “do the thing at 8pm” and then I’ll have to manually set the time and date. 

Most other apps are capable of doing it, so why not this one? 

I’m sure someone will say it’s the “purists” choice, and means we have to be more intentional in our task management, blah, blah, blah…but that’s just an excuse for poor UX. 

It is a maddening design choice and I cannot think of any reason what’s why it is not possible in this app. 

Such a shame.

title: The best on the market, but could still be better
body:
In many ways a superb app, but my main gripe is the lack of a ‘Time’ concept, both for scheduling and deadline purposes. 

I understand that this is an uncritical implementation of ‘Getting Things Done’ methodology. But I would argue that GTD philosophy is flawed, and that in practice, this uncritical implementation makes for a limited user experience.

Some tasks only become actionable after a certain time of day but can remain actionable for days or even months thereafter. For example: I will only be able to book something for a non-specific date after I finish speaking to Person A at midday today, so don’t want this task surfaced to me as actionable this morning whilst I’m commuting to meet them.

Others tasks are actionable from their inception, but ultimately have very specific time deadlines, which would be helpful to see in the user interface, especially as this deadline approaches. For example: I will need to submit a document by 13:00 five months from now, and because it won’t take long to submit I am minded to leave it until much nearer the time because I’ve got a stack of other non-deadlined tasks that I’d like to prioritise. 

Separate to my Time gripe, 
I would value more sophisticated filtering options of my various list views, including the option to filter by tasks that do ‘NOT’ have a certain label attached to them. This would save the proliferation of unnecessary additional filters and lists.

title: Life changing
body:
I purchased this app for iPhone and Mac at the start of this year as part of an ongoing attempt to get a handle on my workflow. I work two jobs while pursuing a career in  acting and, as a result, I have a lot of things to do in a lot of different categories at any given time. 

I tried pen and paper but those to do lists are inflexible and time consuming so were never a long term solution. I became dependent on the built in reminders app but this resulted in a single unwieldy list where some items would stay for months at a time. 

‘Things’ is the answer. With this app I can sit down every month or so, decide what I want to get done, make to do lists and then, this is the improtant bit, set a date for each specific ‘to do’. The result is that you wake up every morning with a curated list of what you need to be getting on with which also includes your calendar events for the day. 

Widgets are great, the ui is incredible, the cloud updates in an instant so I can access and edit my lists seamlessly on both devices.

And, best of all, it’s a one off payment. I hate ‘subscribing’ to software and am really pleased ‘things’ doesn’t indulge in this business model. I can’t recommend the app enough.

body: I never write app reviews but I can’t overstate how happy I am with this product - even with the large (one-off) fee. I’ve been looking for a product like this for a long time but was put off by the cost of Things 3 but I followed other reviewers advice and went online to the website and set up a two week free trial. The set-up process took about three hours to capture and organise all my commitments and I felt immensely relieved at the end of it. After a few days, I was convinced enough to buy the product outright. Two weeks later and my brain no longer has obligations rattling around in it and I’m getting through work at a great rate because tasks are already there to do. Highly recommend this product.

author: Dgbmcc

title: Brilliant but crying out for new features.
body:
I really do love Things 3, I have it for Mac and iPhone and use everyday. It has been too long since there’s been any significant feature upgrades now, would be great if you shared your roadmap. 

The ability to upload images/files would be super helpful. 

The ability to forward iMessages into the app in the same way as spark emails can be. 

Location based reminders would be a helpful.

A calendar view with time blocking feature would be helpful. (I like that ical inputs pull through) but would be good to see Things inputs alongside iCal inputs on a Things calendar view. 

Moving the move, tag and time/date buttons to the top would save having to scroll to the bottom of a long entry that has been forwarded from email. This is a frustrating UX experience. 

Please give us a clue on what’s being worked on, I’m sure it would result in more sales.

title: Very good app
body:
I love this app and have been using it for a couple of years, religiously every day. 

It’s easy to use, quick to use, and a joy to use. It enables me to organise my life and work, and ensure I don’t forget anything I need to do, nor spend all day organising it. 

My only suggestions are two-fold:
1) swipe down from Today to lead into Upcoming, so I can see what’s next
2) I’m not going to lie, it’s expensive. I have it for iPhone and iPad (and you have to pay twice) but I haven’t quite stomached the money to get the Mac version yet. That said, you only pay once, no subscription required, so it works out as good value in the long run. 

I probably will eventually purchase the Mac app for my new MacBook Pro as it is that good!
author: Johnnyjibbs

title: Disappointing features
body:
I bought the product expecting it to simultaneously install on my iPad, but no, the iPhone version only works on the phone and the iPad version is double the price. 🙄. I’m not sure if you need one license per device either. 

Next when I imported my calendar, and made a correction on the original calendar, the correction did not trickle through. 

Finally, I note that had I paid extra for the iPad version, synchjng isn’t via iCloud, but their own cloud and so I’ll worried about data security. 

To summarise, a disappointing app that I’ve uninstalled and asked for a refund that’s been denied by the developer so now I’ve approached Apple. 

Beware.

title: What am I missing? No NLP, no shared lists, no …
body:
I tried Things3 a couple of years ago and asked for a refund as it was lacking a few essential functionalities such as natural language, shared lists, etc. So I went to Todoist and later TickTick.

Couple of years later, tried it again and SHOCKED to find nothing seems to have changed. The AppStore blurb still calls it all new except it’s been “all new” for a few years now. Aside from that, still no natural language entry, still no shared lists, no integrations, etc.

I’m summary, nice UI still (if a little dated) but far far away from the features of competitors such as Todoist and TickTick. 

Oh and the whole buying separate apps for different devices is bizarre. I mean I get that it’s a one-time cost but given there has been very little development over the years, I’d happily pay a subscription if it means the team and afford to remain up to date.

body: This is a bit of a meh app. Looks nice, but functionality is lacking. Tag implementation is woeful as it has been from the days of Things 2. No smart lists or saved searches, which is the biggest let down. Add to that no ability to prioritise your tasks (no, a star is not prioritisation) makes this the hardest task manager to manage your tasks. If you don't work by areas a huge chunk of organisation is lost and it's not easy to repurpose. As nice as it looks, I find it hard work to narrow things down and to organise the way that works for me. CulturedCode have one way of managing tasks. If you're not happy doing it their way then you won't like this inflexible app.

title: Fantastic tool, can it do more?
body:
This is my most used app across my devices, helping manage projects, to-dos and generally organising my work life. The streamlined interface and simple design really allow your tasks to be front and centre. 

There are some things that I’d love to see come to future versions of the app:
- the ability to add headings within areas, just like you can in projects. This would be really useful to separate out tasks within areas that don’t fall in to a specific project
- expand the ‘Today’ and ‘This Evening’ feature so include ‘This Morning’ and ‘This Afternoon’. This would help to better layout a day of tasks
- finally, the ability to create templates for projects. I have several projects that occur regularly, and while I have a template set up, this exists as just another project in the app. It would be great to have a separate menu or filter to store these templates

I can’t fault the app, these are ideas that could take it even further

title: Close to perfect with room for improvement
body:
I seldom write reviews on the App Store unless an app is truly exceptional and Things 3 is just one of those apps. Truthfully, if I could I’d give this app 4.5/5 if that were possible, but docking an entire star for the reasons I have feels a bit unfair considering the impact it’s had on my daily life. Perhaps you have reservations about the price tag; I did too but I’m pleased to say it was worth every penny. It’s perhaps the only app that has actually increased my productivity almost instantaneously. I used to use Evernote for my todo list and I noticed that even though I was writing things down, I wasn’t getting them done. Instead they’d just sit there often getting lost as I made newer notes. Because Things is designed to get you completing tasks instead of just writing about them, there are powerful features to support this, such as badges that tell you how many tasks you have for the day when you aren’t in the app, and easy ways of creating new tasks and moving them around. It removes a lot of the anxiety that comes from having a busy day and not knowing what to tackle first. 
That being said, no app is perfect and I have three key suggestions for the developers on where to improve. 

- It would be great if there were some kind of quick swipe action or even a button to quickly move something to tomorrow. 

- Being able to select anytime in the same menu as someday when changing the date of a task would be very useful (currently the only way is to go to search, type anytime, then tap anytime when it comes up, which isn’t very intuitive). 

- Badges show up for everything you have to do today, regardless of whether it set to today or this evening. it would be good if there were a way to add a custom rule to badge count to only display badges based on the time of day (e.g) you have 3 todos today, 4 this evening making 7 in total. Instead of showing 7, there should be an option to show 3, then 4 later.

So I did have three things but the excellent customer support told me how to use the slightly hidden intelligent language parsing in the date picker. So two of three minor issues solved. Great first class customer support too. 
So that leaves the most annoying issue for me, which is task order in the today list, or the upcoming list for that matter. There should be the choice to order these by time of reminder as well as date (in the upcoming list’s case it does group tasks by due day but not reminder time). It especially annoys me on the today list. Just an option in settings to turn on sorting by reminder time would be perfect for me. Personally I’d like to have no due time tasks first in today then tasks with a due time below in order of due time getting later towards the bottom of the list. Having to keep manually reordering things each day is a little tiresome. It’s good that I’m reviewing all the tasks each morning but still, some automation for list order would be super useful and would personally save me that extra little bit of time. 

But other than this grumble I love the app. Fav task management app that I use daily for personal and work tasks. The Apple Watch app integration is great too.

title: Best UI but needs a day planning feature!
body:
One of the best and most mature todo apps with a great intuitive UI. Very few other options out there with native Mac/iOS apps and so many features.

The only problem is : the latest research shows that the most successful and productive people don’t use todo apps, they use calendars (google it) ! If doesn’t get scheduled, it won’t happen as reliably. Plus, a calendar keeps you honest and realistic as to how many things you can schedule in a day, which helps avoid the « never ending todo list of doom » problem.

Things allows you to schedule tasks to a day only, and even though it now has a reminder feature, this is not enough : there is no notion of task duration, and no way to simply drag a task to a specific space on your day, so you can instantly visualize it.

There are some other apps based on this concept (Plan, Sorted, TickTick) but they’re nowhere near as feature rich. If Things added that one feature, it would completely eat this market !

Things 3 has a sweet new UI and interaction model, but it's not necessarily more efficient. For example, you can no longer reschedule a to-do directly from the Today view in the iOS app; you have to move it to your Inbox first. EDIT: It turns out you can do this by swiping the to-do right, but it's not very discoverable.

The Logbook view needs some serious performance optimisation because scrolling through the thousands of to-dos I've accumulated during eight years is much slower than it was in Things 2. Finally, add in that the developers have ignored a simple question I have asked (twice) on Twitter and the financial investment begins to sting a bit.

title: Devil's advocate
body:
The new Things is clearly a powerful and sleek beast . I haven't though seen many reviews of Things iOS that mention downsides . I do wonder how anyone can assess a new app thoroughly enough to confidently award 5 stars, within days of its release . To perhaps redress the balance (or is it an 'outpouring of negativity'), here are my rough jottings of aspects of Things 3 that I find a turn off:
Loss of functionality from Things 2 as listed in the Things Support article e.g. Projects list gone, can no longer set an advance warning of a deadline, can no longer filter by 'no tag', nor by deadline, cannot change font size, no time stamp inside to-dos. Plus:
No alphabetical sort of projects in sidebar
No collapsing of areas in "sidebar "
Spotlight integration is gone.
Additionally:
No collapsing of the new headings within projects 
Loss of shading impedes ease of the "form filling " aspect of using the app. Things 2 had a superb UI design, attractive and guiding  the user 's eye. We now have white space 
Loss of colour coding of areas - no green icons, except in Someday 
No location-based to dos 
Still no repeating to dos in projects 
Too much white space on the screen ( see above). It's harsh on the eye and creates glare.
Things 3 "What's new" says " When you open a to-do, it smoothly transforms into a clear white piece of paper, ready for your thoughts. " A blank canvas may be helpful if I'm writing a book or a journal, but Things is essentially a database and I find the structure of a form helpful when entering data.
Notes still cannot be hidden
No undo or cancel button e.g. Creating a new to do
I have difficulty in moving around the app - I'm not finding it intuitive 
You can't switch to landscape view  (being locked in portrait feels claustrophobic to me)
The new 'headings' feature looks quite useful, but what is its intended purpose? If it's really defining a sub-task, why can't you mark it 'done'?
The checklist feature is rather in the same category. Nifty, but isn't it really a sub-task? I can't figure out how to archive a checklist for future use, a feature that would be very handy and would justify the use of the term 'checklist'.
The very useful improvements and new features of Things 3 have probably all been covered in the avalanche of positive reviews, so I won't mention them here. It is a good app in many ways , but a long way (in my view) from being brilliant . It is a surprise to me that I much prefer Things 2! Having said that, my 2 star marking is tongue-in-cheek - or just plain cheek! - the app is much better than that. But when you're the devil's advocate, needs must😊. I hope the developer will enhance and improve the features of Things 3, to build on the excellent work they have already done.

title: Polished, practical and nearly perfect
body:
I'd always struggled a bit with Things 2; while I liked the idea the workflow seemed a bit clunky  times and never really clicked (too much tapping at fields and menus). As a result I ended up abandoning it after a few months. 

Things 3 changes all that; the interface is really polished and fluid and you can create new todos and move them around really easily. The redesigned interface lays out information clearly, and animations which both make the app a pleasure to use and highlight important information.  It's pretty much the most polished app I've used - every pixel and animation has clearly been obsessed over.

No app is perfect, though and there are a couple of things that I'd like to see, particularly:

- A fully featured extension (at the moment it just adds the todo to the inbox which is fine but I'd like to select where they go).
- Repeating to dos in projects: at the moment they exist in areas. I heard that this would be changed in a future update. 
- And finally the natural language entry box is a bit hidden. Had to read the manual to find it (pull down on the date selector to get  the entry box). 

To do apps are a personal thing; what works well for me might be to rigid or too unstructured for someone else. Things is flexible enough to be used as a strict GTD app or more causally as a general list of things to do.  I've tried pretty much every major to do app, from Omnifocus to ToDoist and after a month or so of use (I was in the beta for a bit) Things is the one I'm going to stick with.
